RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Focusing on the panel's gender composition without concrete evidence of bias will undermine your professional credibility. All-female panels are common and not legal or procedural evidence of discrimination; members are typically selected based on administrative role or availability. 

While your credentials are strong, hiring decisions for headships depend heavily on interview performance, stakeholder fit, references, and institutional vision. The successful candidate's ten years of classroom experience and leadership coursework may have matched their immediate strategic needs. 

Do not raise bias based on demographics alone. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting your written feedback. Once received, review the objective scoring rubrics and rationale before concluding that sex played any role.
